newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZAPMB declines Apple Fields export application.
newsitem.headline: NZAPMB declines Apple Fields export application.

text.p: The New Zealand Apple and Pear Marketing Board said on Tuesday it had declined an application by Apple Fields for an export licence.
"The proposal fails to meet the export consent guidelines which were developed in consultation with the industry," Chairman John McCliskie said in a statement.
"The proposal aimed to benefit the applicants. It would have cost the rest of the industry," he said.
To succeed, applications have to increase the total net income brought in by New Zealand apples and must be complementary to the industry's export business and strategy.
"Apple Fields' application failed on those two key grounds," McCliskie said.
Apple Fields said in mid November it would bulldoze all of its trees and quit the pipfruit business unless it was granted an export licence for a proposed new joint venture.
The company, which also has interests in the dairy industry through subsidiary Dairy Brands would become a property development and investment company.

Apple Fields argued that the major joint venture, with four leading fruit distributors in the United States, Europe and Asia, would integrate the total process from orchard to final distribution, through a variety of brands, to supermarkets throughout the northern hemisphere.

The company, which posted a loss of NZ$2 million in the half year to March and expects a significant operating loss for the full year, blames the NZAPMB for its poor economic performance. The directors argue the decline in profitability will be arrested if Apple Fields exports its own fruit.
The company said the joint venture was budgeted to earn NZ$28.5 million, compared with a maximum of $15.2 million apple Fields would be paid by the NZAPMB for the same crop.

Apple Fields is no stranger to the anti-monopoly game, having railed for years against the NZAPMB's control over pipfruit exports. The company has been granted permission to export a maximum of 59,000 cartons of apples in the past, but its main applications have been rejected.
Under the latest application Apple Fields wanted to export its total crop, around 1.5 million cartons.
